intervals.label: WIMP-search data runs at the Stanford Underground Facility
intervals.note: Start: the earliest report read (TAUP97, Sept 1997; arXiv Dec 1997) says 'we have begun taking data to search for WIMPs' and mentions data runs over 'the past year', so data taking began in 1996-97; the exact start is not published in the sources read, and 1997 is a year-level upper bound. End: the last CDMS I data, the Ge BLIP run 'Between November, 1998, and September, 1999'.
intervals.quote: we have begun taking data to search for WIMPs

intervals.label: completed (last CDMS I data run)
intervals.note: Month precision; the date is the end of the last CDMS I data set analysed (Sept 1999), not a published closing date. The first tower of ZIP detectors (CDMS II) was commissioned at SUF in the second half of 2001 (arXiv:1010.4290) and moved to Soudan in 2003.
intervals.quote: Between November, 1998, and September, 1999, 96 live days of data were obtained using 3 of 4 165 g Ge BLIP detectors.

placements.note: Years/months as for the experiment intervals.
placements.quote: The first stage of the Cryogenic Dark Matter Search (CDMS I) operates at the Stanford Underground Facility, a tunnel 10.6 m beneath the Stanford University campus.

depth.note: Later papers give ~16 m of water (arXiv:astro-ph/0203500, astro-ph/0002471).
depth.quote: at a depth of 17 meters water-equivalent (mwe)

target_mass.note: Mass of each Ge BLIP detector; four BLIPs in the 1999 run, three analysed. A 100 g Si ZIP detector ran in 1998.
target_mass.quote: Between November, 1998, and September, 1999, 96 live days of data were obtained using 3 of 4 165 g Ge BLIP detectors.

summary.plain: The first stage of the Cryogenic Dark Matter Search: germanium and silicon crystals cooled to 20 thousandths of a degree above absolute zero, in a shallow tunnel under Stanford University. Its 2000 result excluded, at more than 84% confidence, the whole dark matter signal region reported by the DAMA experiment.
summary.technical: Four 165 g Ge BLIP (NTD phonon) detectors and a 100 g Si ZIP detector measuring ionization and phonons, in a 20 mK cold volume behind 15 cm Pb, 25 cm polyethylene and a scintillator muon veto at ~17 m.w.e. (Stanford Underground Facility). 1998 Si run (33 live days) and 1998-99 Ge run (96 live days, 3 of 4 detectors; 10.6 kg d after cuts, 15.8 kg d in the later relaxed-fiducial analysis). Limits exclude unexplored space for 10-70 GeV/c^2; 23 candidates consistent with neutron background.

technology.quote: CDMS detectors measure phonon and electron-hole pair production to determine recoil energy and ionization yield for each event.
technology.value: Cryogenic Ge (BLIP) and Si (ZIP) detectors measuring phonons and ionization simultaneously
